prompt: You followed the frontend track and `node --version` prints `v22.22.0`. What does this course ask you to install before starting?

choices.text: A version manager, so the course can switch Node versions
choices.why: The lesson asks you not to: two copies of Node is how a program ends up on the wrong one.

choices.text: Node.js again, from Ubuntu's own package
choices.why: Ubuntu 24.04's package is Node 18, which Vite 8 refuses.

choices.text: Playwright's browser, before the project exists
choices.why: It is installed in lesson 4, the first one that drives a browser.

choices.text: Nothing yet: the browser comes in lesson 4
choices.why: Right. Node 22 and Git are all lesson 1 needs.

prompt: Why does the course pin every package to one exact version in `package.json`?

choices.text: npm refuses to install a version range such as `^8.3.4`
choices.why: It installs ranges happily; the template asked for one.

choices.text: Exact versions download faster
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: So that what you install is what the lessons recorded
choices.why: Right. A caret lets two people installing on different days get different code.

choices.text: Vite only works with a pinned TypeScript
choices.why: Vite would work with any TypeScript 6.0; pinning is about repeating the setup.

prompt: What is the drawback of a virtual machine with no desktop for this course in particular?

choices.text: There is no screen to show the app on, though the tests still run
choices.why: Right. The browser the tests use needs no window.

choices.text: Node.js does not run on Ubuntu Server
choices.why: It does; the course was recorded on Ubuntu 24.04.

choices.text: npm cannot reach the registry from inside a virtual machine's network
choices.why: A virtual machine has a network like any computer.

choices.text: Git needs a graphical editor for commits
choices.why: `git commit -m` needs no editor at all.

prompt: Where must `courses.json` be for the planner to fetch it from `/courses.json`?

choices.text: In `src/`, beside `main.ts`
choices.why: Vite transforms what is in `src/` and serves nothing there at the root.

choices.text: In `public/`
choices.why: Right. Vite serves `public/` at the site's root, as it is.

choices.text: In `node_modules/`, where npm keeps the files
choices.why: That folder holds installed packages, and Git ignores it.

choices.text: Anywhere, if `index.html` links to it
choices.why: `index.html` does not link to it; `main.ts` fetches it by address.

prompt: Using the planner's data, how many minutes are planned in the week of Monday 19 to Sunday 25 October 2026, counting every course?
hint: Four sessions fall in that week: 45, 60, 30 and 25 minutes.

prompt: `addSession` is given a plan and returns a plan. What happens to the plan it was given?

choices.text: The new session is pushed onto its `sessions` array
choices.why: That would change the caller's plan behind its back; the function builds a new array.

choices.text: It is saved to `courses.json`
choices.why: Nothing writes to the file; a plan lives in memory until lesson 5.

choices.text: It is emptied, and the new plan replaces it
choices.why: It is left alone.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. It returns a new plan and leaves the old one as it was.

prompt: A session's date is stored as the text `2026-10-21`. Why can `weekTotal` compare two of them with `>=` and `<=`?

choices.text: TypeScript turns strings that look like dates into `Date` objects before comparing them
choices.why: TypeScript converts nothing at runtime; its types are removed.

choices.text: JavaScript compares strings by their length
choices.why: It compares them character by character.

choices.text: Fixed-width parts, largest first, sort as text in calendar order
choices.why: Right. The most significant part comes first and every part has a fixed width.

choices.text: The comparison only works because all sessions are in 2026
choices.why: It works across years too: 2025-12-31 sorts before 2026-01-01.

prompt: What does `curl http://localhost:5173/src/planner.ts` return while the dev server runs?

choices.text: The TypeScript file exactly as it is on disk
choices.why: The interfaces are gone from what came back.

choices.text: An error, because a browser cannot ask for a `.ts` file
choices.why: It can ask; Vite answers with JavaScript.

choices.text: JavaScript, with the types removed
choices.why: Right. A browser runs JavaScript and nothing else.

choices.text: The whole app bundled into one file
choices.why: In development Vite serves each module on its own; bundling is `npm run build`.

prompt: Why are the planner's weekly totals all 0 when you open it in most weeks?

choices.text: This week comes from the computer's clock; the data is October 2026
choices.why: Right. Lesson 4 sets the browser's clock so a test gets the same answer every day.

choices.text: `courses.json` failed to load, so no course has sessions to add up
choices.why: Then the page would say it could not load your courses.

choices.text: `weekTotal` only counts sessions marked done
choices.why: It counts every session in the week, done or not.

choices.text: The dev server strips the numbers out of the data
choices.why: Vite serves `public/` as it is.

prompt: Which of these does `src/main.ts` do? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: fetches `/courses.json`
choices.why: Before anything is drawn.

choices.text: draws again when the address after `#` changes
choices.why: It listens for `hashchange`.

choices.text: saves new sessions to the file
choices.why: A plan lives in memory; reload and it is back to the file.

choices.text: says so when the data cannot be loaded
choices.why: "Could not load your courses."

items: git init, git add -A, git commit

prompt: Match each message to its cause.

pairs.right: the terminal is not in the project's folder

pairs.left: does not provide an export named 'styleText'
Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...
pairs.right: a first dev server is still running

prompt: Vite says `Port 5173 is in use, trying another one...` and starts on 5174. Why does the lesson call that a trap rather than an error?

choices.text: Because port 5174 is reserved for the operating system and its own services
choices.why: It is an ordinary free port.

choices.text: Everything works, on a port your open tab and lesson 4's tests are not using
choices.why: Right. A tab still at 5173 talks to the other server.

choices.text: Because the second server serves an old copy of the files
choices.why: Both serve the same folder.

choices.text: Because Vite exits a few seconds later
choices.why: It keeps running, which is why it goes unnoticed.

prompt: A fresh clone of the project has no `node_modules`. Why does the lesson rebuild it with `npm ci` rather than `npm install`?

choices.text: `npm install` cannot read a lockfile
choices.why: It reads it, and may also update it.

choices.text: `npm ci` downloads from a faster mirror
choices.why: Both use the same registry.

choices.text: `npm install` would delete `package.json`
choices.why: It never deletes it.

choices.text: It installs exactly what the lockfile says, and refuses if `package.json` disagrees
choices.why: Right. Repeating a setup is the point; quietly bringing the two into line is not.

prompt: Which line of the `styleText` failure tells you the cause?

choices.text: The path inside `node_modules/rolldown`
choices.why: That is where it failed, not why.

choices.text: `Node.js v18.19.1`, the last one
choices.why: Right. Vite 8 needs Node 20.19 or later.

choices.text: `SyntaxError`, which means your code has a typo
choices.why: The syntax error is in a package, on a Node too old for it.

choices.text: `> vite`, because the script name is wrong
choices.why: The script is right; it starts and then fails.

prompt: What does a test pyramid say?

choices.text: Exactly how many tests of each kind a project must have
choices.why: It is about proportions and cost, not quotas.

choices.text: Where testing effort is cheapest, and what to have most of
choices.why: Right. It is an argument about money.

choices.text: That end-to-end tests are not worth writing
choices.why: They are its tip: few, and kept for what only they can find.

choices.text: That unit tests give more confidence in the whole than any other kind
choices.why: Confidence in the whole grows towards the top.

prompt: Match each shape or layer to what it adds.

pairs.right: most tests at the unit level
the widest band in the middle
the whole app in a real browser

prompt: A form reads the wrong field and the total never changes, though `weekTotal` is correct. Which kind of test, among the four, finds this soonest?

choices.text: A unit test of `weekTotal`
choices.why: It passes: the function is correct.

choices.text: The type checker, `tsc`
choices.why: Reading the wrong field can be perfectly well typed.

choices.text: An end-to-end test, since only a browser shows a form
choices.why: It would find it too, later and more slowly; jsdom has forms.

choices.text: A component test that types into the form and reads the total
choices.why: Right. The fault is between the pieces, and that layer sees pieces together without a browser.

prompt: Test each thing at the ___ level that can see it fail.
Match each file of the planner to the lowest layer that can see it fail.
Why can a component test in jsdom not tell you that a button is hidden behind another element?

choices.text: jsdom has no buttons
choices.why: It has every HTML element.

choices.text: jsdom runs too fast to see it
choices.why: Speed is not what is missing.

choices.text: jsdom computes no layout
choices.why: Right. Without layout, nothing is anywhere, so nothing covers anything.

choices.text: The button was created with `createElement` rather than markup
choices.why: How it was created makes no difference to jsdom.

prompt: Why does the lesson want the fast part of the suite to stay fast?

choices.text: A suite people do not run before committing catches nothing
choices.why: Right. Speed is what makes people run it.

choices.text: Because CI services charge by the test, and slow tests cost more
choices.why: They charge by time at most; that is not the argument.

choices.text: Because slow tests are always wrong
choices.why: Slow tests can be right; the end-to-end ones are slow and needed.

choices.text: Because Vitest stops after two seconds
choices.why: It has no such limit.

prompt: Without the `Number(…)`, `tsc` refuses `data.get("minutes")` as an argument to `addSession`. What would have happened at runtime without the checker?

choices.text: The browser would have converted the string to a number
choices.why: Nothing converts it; `Number.isInteger("15")` is false.

choices.text: The form would reject 15 as not a whole number
choices.why: Right. The string "15" fails `Number.isInteger`, and the person sees the error.

choices.text: The page would not load at all
choices.why: It loads; the mistake shows only when the form is used.

choices.text: Nothing: JavaScript has no difference between "15" and 15
choices.why: It does, and `Number.isInteger` is one place that shows it.

prompt: `courses.json` is edited to say `"minutes": "45"`. Does `tsc --noEmit` catch it?

choices.text: Yes, because `Session` declares `minutes` as a number
choices.why: The declaration is not checked against data that arrives at runtime.

choices.text: Yes, because Vite type-checks files in `public/`
choices.why: Vite serves `public/` as it is and checks nothing.

choices.text: No: `response.json()` is typed as anything, and `main.ts` takes it on trust
choices.why: Right. Data from outside needs a check at runtime.

choices.text: Only if the file is renamed `courses.ts`
choices.why: Renaming is not how a fetched file gets checked.

prompt: What does `npx tsc --noEmit` print when the project type-checks?

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. Silence is the pass.

choices.text: `0 errors`
choices.why: It prints nothing at all.

choices.text: The list of files it checked
choices.why: Not without extra options.

choices.text: The JavaScript it would have written
choices.why: `--noEmit` writes none.

prompt: A test checks that the list item's class is `session done` after a click. What is wrong with it?

choices.text: Classes cannot be read from a test, only from a browser's devtools
choices.why: They can; that is the problem.

choices.text: Renaming the class breaks it, and nobody sees a change
choices.why: Right. It describes the code rather than the behaviour.

choices.text: It runs too slowly
choices.why: Speed is not its problem.

choices.text: A click cannot be simulated in jsdom, so the test never runs
choices.why: It can; lesson 3 does it.

prompt: Why is a week with one session a poor test of `weekTotal`?

choices.text: Vitest needs at least two values to compare
choices.why: It compares one value with another; one session is fine for that.

choices.text: Totals of one are rounded to zero
choices.why: Nothing is rounded.

choices.text: It cannot tell adding apart from copying, nor a week cut short at either end
choices.why: Right. Data that can fail is data with sessions at the edges.

choices.text: A week with one session does not exist in `courses.json`
choices.why: The week before and the week after each have one.

prompt: Which of these are worth testing in the planner? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: that `addSession` refuses 0 minutes
choices.why: A rule the planner decided.

choices.text: that `document.createElement("li")` makes an `li`
choices.why: That is the browser's code, not yours.

choices.text: that pressing Add session shows the new total
choices.why: The wiring in `view.ts`.

choices.text: that Vite serves the files in `public/`
choices.why: Vite's job, tested by Vite.
